evidence.title: As midterms approach, Republican candidates weigh how closely to align with Trump

occurrences.checkable_against: Keith Schipper statement and 2024 Republican platform
occurrences.quote_span: “The president has delivered on the agenda he promised voters in 2024 and Republicans are smartly using it to win this year.”
occurrences.speaker: Keith Schipper
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Rally video or event records and 2024 presidential election results by congressional district
occurrences.quote_span: Rep. Mike Lawler, a New York Republican who represents a district carried by Kamala Harris in the last election, appeared on stage with the president during a rally in his district just three months ago.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign website
occurrences.quote_span: That section now says he is running because he “believes America needs more servant leaders and fewer corrupt politicians” and “because he’s not finished serving the country he loves.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign website
occurrences.quote_span: While De La Cruz no longer touts himself as a “TRUMP CONSERVATIVE” at the top of his homepage, a video that is embedded lower down features the Air Force veteran speaking at a Trump rally.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Keith Schipper statement and Marty O'Donnell campaign materials
occurrences.quote_span: O'Donnell adviser Keith Schipper noted that O'Donnell, a music composer best known for his work on the “Halo” video game series, has not deviated from his steadfast support for Trump.
occurrences.speaker: Keith Schipper
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Mike Barrett campaign materials, House election results, and War Powers voting record
occurrences.quote_span: In Michigan, Rep. Barrett, who flipped a Lansing-area district two years ago, has been highlighting his vote against Trump’s war in Iran on the campaign trail as he competes against William Lawrence, a self-described democratic socialist.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Ralph Alvarado campaign website archives
occurrences.quote_span: He now promises to offer “INDEPENDENT LEADERSHIP” after previously running as an “AMERICA FIRST FIGHTER.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Marty O'Donnell campaign website archive
occurrences.quote_span: The words “President Trump endorsed Marty O'Donnell” were written beneath the image.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Republican congressional candidate campaign websites and public statements
occurrences.quote_span: the slight shift among at least a half-dozen Republican congressional candidates could signal the beginning of a more significant move within the party
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Ralph Alvarado campaign website media gallery and campaign statement
occurrences.quote_span: Campaign manager Andy Westberry noted Trump's photo still appears elsewhere in a media gallery.
occurrences.speaker: Andy Westberry
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Marty O'Donnell campaign website archives
occurrences.quote_span: In Nevada, Republican congressional candidate Marty O'Donnell's website featured Trump prominently in June.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Jordan Pawlicki campaign statement and Carlos De La Cruz campaign website
occurrences.quote_span: “Carlos is honored to have President Trump’s support, which is why the President is featured prominently across our website,” Pawlicki said.
occurrences.speaker: Jordan Pawlicki
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign statement or interview records
occurrences.quote_span: De La Cruz's campaign rejected any suggestion he was backing away from the president
occurrences.speaker: Carlos De La Cruz campaign
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Marty O'Donnell campaign website
occurrences.quote_span: Two months later, the photo does not appear on the website.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Marty O'Donnell campaign statement and website change logs
occurrences.quote_span: O'Donnell's campaign said the photo was not intentionally removed; the change was simply the standard rotation of the “splash page.”
occurrences.speaker: Marty O'Donnell campaign
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: 2026 Republican candidate campaign materials and midterm ballot records
occurrences.quote_span: The overwhelming majority of Republicans on the ballot this fall are embracing Trump despite his dismal approval ratings , an unpopular war with Iran and lingering inflation.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Eric Flores campaign homepage archives
occurrences.quote_span: Eric Flores, a former assistant U.S. Attorney and Texas Army National Guard infantry captain running against Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez Jr. in South Texas, once featured “SUPPORT PRESIDENT TRUMP’S AGENDA” as No. 2 in his list of priorities on his campaign homepage. That item has now been replaced with “ LOWER THE COST OF LIVING ,” a top issue for voters.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Nick Begich campaign homepage archive
occurrences.quote_span: In June, he highlighted his relationship to Trump on the homepage of his website
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Keith Schipper statement
occurrences.quote_span: “Republicans are embracing President Trump on the campaign trail because they know he is the key to getting his voters out in November,” Schipper said.
occurrences.speaker: Keith Schipper
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign website
occurrences.quote_span: He still calls himself a “TEXAS TRUMP CONSERVATIVE” on his bio page and lists “Supporting President Trump’s America First Agenda” as among his priorities on a “Mission” page.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Andy Westberry campaign statement
occurrences.quote_span: “The socialists are going to have to do a lot better than this nonsense to win this district,” he said in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Andy Westberry
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign website archives
occurrences.quote_span: It once described him as “ready to be President Trump’s wingman in Congress.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Jordan Pawlicki campaign statement and archived De La Cruz website
occurrences.quote_span: De La Cruz campaign manager Jordan Pawlicki said in a statement that, during the primary, several candidates were claiming the president’s endorsement, so the campaign “put it front and center.”
occurrences.speaker: Jordan Pawlicki
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Carlos De La Cruz campaign website archives
occurrences.quote_span: The all-caps headline on Texas Republican congressional candidate Carlos De La Cruz's website used to align him with President Donald Trump. Not anymore.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson statement
occurrences.quote_span: Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee, called it a “manufactured storyline.”
occurrences.speaker: Mike Marinella
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Ralph Alvarado campaign homepage archives and May 2026 primary materials
occurrences.quote_span: In Kentucky, Ralph Alvarado, running to represent the overwhelmingly Republican 6th Congressional District, removed all references to Trump from his campaign homepage , as well as a photo of the two of them together after winning his primary in May.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson statement
occurrences.quote_span: “President Trump and House Republicans have delivered historic results for the American people, and our candidates are eager to take that record directly to voters alongside the President on the campaign trail,” he said.
occurrences.speaker: Mike Marinella
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Associated Press reporter correspondence records
occurrences.quote_span: Begich's campaign did not respond to a request for comment.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates

occurrences.checkable_against: Nick Begich campaign homepage archives
occurrences.quote_span: In June, he highlighted his relationship to Trump on the homepage of his website: “Alongside President Trump, we have made great gains for Alaska, putting us on a path to self-determination and generational success.” This week, nothing in that section has been changed, except for the opening line that previously mentioned Trump. Now, that line reads, “We have delivered for Alaska, putting us on a path to self-determination and generational success.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Republican congressional candidates
